industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried, with the tape now agreeing: Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, A prior, the sharpest fall in technology, where last week's reading still ranked the sector B. The two conditions for Neutral (the AI credit channel stabilising; a second house joining Jefferies' European call) could not be tested because no strategist reached the pack; the only artificial-intelligence item is an undated headline that low AI exposure is Europe's edge. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Of the Pool's semiconductor names, Technoprobe, AT&S, INFICON, Sensirion, STMicroelectronics, Soitec, AIXTRON and AMS Osram are marked leaving the Pool or meet a Sell Criterion, so the row's cost to the Lists is falling of its own accord. Counter-case: demand was never the problem and European exposure is equipment, power and optics. To C when the AI credit channel is read stable or a second house joins the European call, with relative strength holding C or better.

memo.verdict: PARK at Triaging, medium conviction, on entry point and case complexity rather than on the change force. The memo refuses progression to Early-Stage Assessment now and places AIXA-DE on a quarterly watch list with four named re-activation triggers: (1) a visible gallium nitride datacentre tool order tied to 800-volt high-voltage direct-current rack architecture; (2) western power fab utilisation crossing 70% and heading to 80%; (3) evidence the second-half 2026 shipment ramp of over EUR 385m actually landed; (4) a Hyperion three-hundred-millimetre design win at a tier-one power integrated device manufacturer. A separate price-based re-test fires on a close below the 200-day moving average of EUR 33.21, which re-opens the entry-point objection independently of the fundamental triggers. The memo explicitly ADOPTS the Risks family's own stage recommendation of "a strict hold-and-watch stance rather than proceeding with immediate allocation" and treats park as the Triaging-stage equivalent. Next scheduled re-run: within five working days of the Q3 2026 print, expected late October 2026.
case: The case for parking runs in four steps, each anchored to a graded Element.

Step one, the change force is real and should not be dismissed. Element E1 RA1 grades [B] and its first Core Question grades [A]. Artificial-intelligence datacentres are migrating from copper to optical interconnect, forcing indium phosphide laser capacity build-out and therefore deposition-tool demand. AIXTRON captures that wave almost completely: near-100% share of indium phosphide deposition tools and 98 of 100 recent optoelectronics tool orders. NVIDIA committed a combined USD 4.0bn to Coherent and Lumentum, and Lumentum placed multiple G10-AsP orders on 19 May 2026. Roughly fifteen laser companies globally are reserving delivery slots ahead of 2027 fab expansions, which materially reduces single-customer dependence. Internal change forces are also live: the G10 platform is 70% of optoelectronics system sales against 10% in FY24 and carries gross margins around 50%; a EUR 40m Penang plant adds 20% capacity toward EUR 1.2bn of revenue capacity; two headcount rounds inside fifteen months deliver roughly one percentage point of structural margin; and the EUR 450m convertible lifted liquidity to EUR 816.2m. The memo is explicit that the park is not a quality judgement on the business.

Step two, the base underneath the force is not robust. Element E1 RA2 grades [D]. Six live external headwinds are documented, four of them outside management control: silicon carbide customer utilisation near 50% with no tool order recovery expected before 2027 and power equipment investment contracting for a fourth consecutive year; hyperscaler 800-volt adoption pushed from 2027 to 2028; Veeco's Propel three-hundred-millimetre pilot-line order in late 2025 plus over USD 250m of indium phosphide tool orders in May 2026; China's self-manufactured equipment share reaching 35% in 2025 with Chinese tools priced 30% to 40% below historical averages; indium phosphide substrate permit backlogs at supplier AXT; and a move to 1.20 dollars per euro costing roughly one percentage point of EBIT margin against a 2026 budget rate set at exactly 1.20. Delivery congruency is mixed: orders and margins have delivered while revenue has not, which the memo identifies as exactly the shape a false-friend setup takes.
counter_case: The memo carried the counter-case at Element level and did not soften it.

The strongest single counter is that a false-friend label is unfalsifiable at the point it is applied. Every genuine multi-year upcycle looks identical to a pull-forward in its first two years. The Risks family's own matrix concedes that the bull profile would clear its inconsistencies if power orders inflect sporadically. The memo rejects this only on the ground that the guardrail does not require certainty, merely that the pattern is present and unresolved, and that Section E carries the exact trigger that would resolve it.
triggers: Re-activation triggers, any one of which reopens the case. One: a visible gallium nitride datacentre tool order tied to 800-volt high-voltage direct-current rack architecture, the single most diagnostic evidence in the file and the event that would convert the case from one-legged to two-legged. Two: western power fab utilisation crossing 70% and heading to 80%, the level both Deutsche Bank and Jefferies name as the order-trigger gate. Three: evidence the second-half 2026 shipment ramp of over EUR 385m actually landed, which resolves the supplier-constraint and execution objections together. Four: a Hyperion three-hundred-millimetre design win at a tier-one power integrated device manufacturer, which would neutralise the Veeco early-mover threat. Price-based re-test: a close below the 200-day moving average of EUR 33.21 re-opens the entry-point question independently.

Key questions raised for the next stage. Is the optical order wave a multi-year capacity build or a two-year pull-forward, the question every other question is downstream of. What is normalised power-segment earnings power at 80% customer utilisation, without which the second leg cannot be sized. How durable is the switching-cost moat across a wafer-format change, named by the business foundations family as the single largest risk to the franchise. What does the sell-side de-rating from 37 times to 25 times forward earnings actually price, being the difference between a quality re-rating and a quality downgrade. Also: model the gross-margin bridge from 40.7% toward the guided 42% and the 46% forecast for 2028, separating mix from volume absorption; and resolve the activist requisition outcome, unresolved at the memo date.

Carry-forward mechanics. Element E8 primary fit setup is RA2, big demand change-driven earnings upgrade; secondary is RA3, strong corporate change driven upgrade. These two deepen at Early-Stage Assessment under the carve-out; the remaining six Required Attributes and both negative guardrails carry forward at Triaging depth. Elements E2, E3, E4, E9, E10, E12, E13, E18, E19 and E20 are first written at Early-Stage Assessment. Section D Pillar III is first written at Early-Stage Assessment. Watch cadence if no trigger fires: a full re-run at each quarterly print for four quarters, then a decision to retire the name or re-brief the Researcher.

Live process flags. The memo records that context/coverage.md states "Above-floor reports present: none" while a direct listing found six above-floor families on disk, all of which were read. It records five conflict reconciliations rather than silently selecting values: Q1 2026 revenue EUR 59.38m falling 47.20% (interim report) versus EUR 59.0m falling 47.6% (Deutsche Bank); Q2 2026 gross margin 40.6% (Morgan Stanley table) versus 40.7% (reported); FY26 growth framed three ways as 0.61% calculated, 5% per Jefferies and 8% at midpoint; silicon carbide share given as 27%, 35% and 37% across sources; and cash of EUR 224.6m at FY25 versus EUR 272.7m at 31 March 2026, which are different dates rather than a conflict. It flags that Thematics 1, 2 and 3 are marked in the thematics file itself as carried forward and not re-reviewed since 16 April 2026, a currency caveat on those three specifically, with only Thematic 4 current work.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
